Load necessary libraries
```{r}
library(virtualArray)
library(GEOquery)

library(limma)

library(plotly)
library(sva)
library(ggplot2)

```
Download metadata full series.matrix file
```{r}
#Study 1
gse<-getGEO('GSE58144')
gse<-gse[[1]]
phenotype_data<-pData(gse)
geo_accession<- "GSE58144"
```
Download the datasets that once untarred, will reveal the individual txt/CEL files (the raw data we want to use for analysis)
```{r}
#Study 1:
gse_dir <- "<original_archive>/MICROARRAY_DATA/GSE58144"
```

Update phenotype conditions: clearly state "control" or "RIF"
- "title" is the column where the conditions are stated; check this to ensure it aligns with pheno column name
```{r}
phenotype_data <- phenotype_data %>%
  mutate(title = case_when(
    grepl("control", title, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Control",
    grepl("failure", title, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "RIF",
    TRUE ~ title #(Keep original value if neither is matched)
  ))

# Clean the phenotype data to keep only cohort information
phenotype_data <- phenotype_data %>% rename(batch = characteristics_ch1.2)


#Adjusting biospy timing column to include in batch correction
#Rename the column
colnames(phenotype_data)[colnames(phenotype_data) == "characteristics_ch1.3"] <- "biopsy_timing"
#Extract the biopsy timing information from the renamed column (so it only includes the # and not full sentence)
phenotype_data$biopsy_timing <- gsub(".*(\\d+)\\s*days.*", "\\1", phenotype_data$biopsy_timing)
phenotype_data$biopsy_timing <- as.factor(phenotype_data$biopsy_timing)  

```

Read the target 
```{r}
output_dir<-"<original_archive>/MICROARRAY_DATA/GSE58144/txt_files_updated"
txt_files <- list.files(output_dir, pattern = "\\.txt$", full.names = TRUE)

target_file<-"<original_archive>/MICROARRAY_DATA/GSE58144/GSE58144_rawfiles_dye_orientation.txt"
target <- readTargets(target_file)

# Extract GSM accession from the full file names (before the first underscore)
gsm_accessions <- sub("_.*", "", basename(txt_files))

base_names_stripped <- sub("^[^_]*_", "", basename(txt_files))

# Create a data frame that contains the full file name and the GSM accession -> verifies dye swap pairs
gsm_mapping <- data.frame(
  raw_data_file = base_names_stripped,
  GSM = gsm_accessions
)

target <- merge(target, gsm_mapping, by = "raw_data_file", all.x = TRUE)

idx <- match(base_names_stripped, target$raw_data_file)
if (any(is.na(idx))) {
  cat("Some files in txt_files not found in target$raw_data_file:\n")
  print(base_names_stripped[is.na(idx)])
  stop("Cannot align your filenames.")
}

target <- target[idx, ]
stopifnot(identical(base_names_stripped, target$raw_data_file))

```

Read the raw data
```{r}
raw_data <- read.maimages(
  txt_files,
  source = "agilent",
  columns = list(
    R = "Ch2 Signal Mean", 
    G = "Ch1 Signal Mean"),
  annotation = c("Reporter Identifier") 
)

# Rename "Reporter Identifier" -> "ProbeName" for clarity
colnames(raw_data$genes)[
  colnames(raw_data$genes) == "Reporter Identifier"
] <- "ProbeName"

plotDensities(raw_data, main = "Before Background Subtraction")
```
- assess whether the distribution of intensity values is consistent across arrays

Flip the R values for dye swap array
- After this swap, every array in your RGList is standardized so that the same channel (for example, the Red channel) always represents the sample and the Green channel always represents the reference.
```{r}
swap_index <- which(target$Cy3 == "sample" & target$Cy5 == "reference")
temp <- raw_data$R[, swap_index]
raw_data$R[, swap_index] <- raw_data$G[, swap_index]
raw_data$G[, swap_index] <- temp

```

Background correction and normalization
```{r}
bg_corrected_data <- backgroundCorrect(raw_data, method="normexp")
normalized_data <- normalizeWithinArrays(bg_corrected_data, method = "loess")

plotDensities(bg_corrected_data, main = "After Background Subtraction")

#PCA to check results
pca_result <- prcomp(t(normalized_data$M), scale = TRUE) 
phenotype_data$title <- factor(phenotype_data$title)
# Generate colors based on the levels of 'title'
colors <- rainbow(length(levels(phenotype_data$title)))[phenotype_data$title]
# Plot PCA result
plot(pca_result$x[, 1:2], col = colors, pch = 16, main = "PCA Plot")

```
Normalization validation:
- A right-skewed distribution of the A values (log2 of the average intensity) is common in microarray data -> reflects that most probes are not highly expressed and have relatively low intensities in both channels (Cy3 and Cy5)
```{r}
# Histogram of M values
hist(normalized_data$M, main="Distribution of M (Log2 Ratio)", xlab="M")

# Histogram of A values
hist(normalized_data$A, main="Distribution of A (Log2 Average)", xlab="A")
#calculate mean M
mean_M <- mean(normalized_data$M)
print(mean_M)

plot(density(normalized_data$A), main="Density of A values", xlab="A (Log2 Average Intensity)")
```

Averaging log ratios for duplicate GSM (dye swaps)
```{r}
#clean up normalized$M so that we can average the dye swap intensities per sample based on GSM accession
colnames(normalized_data$M) <- gsub(".*/(GSM[0-9]+)_.*", "\\1", colnames(normalized_data$M))

# Average the log ratios based on GSM accession
average_logratios <- avearrays(normalized_data$M, ID = target$GSM)
#Replace the original matrix with the averaged data
normalized_data$M <- average_logratios
```

BATCH CORRECTION
```{r}
# Ensure the corrected expression matrix and phenotype data are aligned
# corrected_expr_timing: genes x samples
normalized_matrix<-as.matrix(normalized_data$M)
expr_matrix <- normalized_matrix[, match(rownames(phenotype_data), colnames(normalized_matrix))]
stopifnot(identical(rownames(phenotype_data), colnames(expr_matrix)))

# Factorize the condition and batch variables
phenotype_data$title <- factor(phenotype_data$title, levels = c("Control", "RIF"))
phenotype_data$batch <- factor(phenotype_data$batch)

# Build a model matrix preserving condition only (the biological signal of interest)
mod <- model.matrix(~ title, data = phenotype_data)

# Run ComBat: This will remove batch effects (and any effects not in mod)
combat_expr <- ComBat(
  dat = expr_matrix,              # Expression matrix (genes x samples)
  batch = phenotype_data$batch,   # Batch variable to remove
  mod = mod,                      # Preserve only the condition effect
  par.prior = TRUE,               # Use parametric adjustments
  prior.plots = FALSE             # Set to TRUE to visualize the priors if desired
)

```

Generate final data frame and annotation
```{r}
# Convert the corrected expression matrix to a data frame
final_df <- as.data.frame(combat_expr)

final_df$ProbeName <- normalized_data$genes$ProbeName
final_df <- merge(final_df, annotation_map, by = "ProbeName", all.x = TRUE)

final_df <- final_df %>% 
  filter(GeneSymbol != "" & !is.na(GeneSymbol))

final_aggregated <- final_df %>%
  group_by(GeneSymbol) %>%
  summarise(across(where(is.numeric), ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE))) %>%
  ungroup()

#Set GeneSymbol as row names if you want:
final_dataframe <- as.data.frame(final_aggregated)
rownames(final_dataframe) <- final_dataframe$GeneSymbol
final_dataframe$GeneSymbol <- NULL

```


PCA for final_dataframe
```{r, fig.height=8, fig.width=10}
pca_data <- final_dataframe
pca_result <- prcomp(t(pca_data), center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)  # transpose to have samples as rows

#Create a PCA scores data frame
pca_scores <- as.data.frame(pca_result$x)
pca_scores$Condition <- phenotype_data$title
pca_scores$Cohort <- phenotype_data$batch
# Assuming phenotype_data has a sample identifier column; if not, use rownames from pca_scores
pca_scores$SampleID <- rownames(pca_scores)

#Plot PCA using ggplot2 with labels for each point
pca_plot <- ggplot(pca_scores, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = Condition, shape = Cohort)) +
  geom_point(size = 4) +
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = SampleID), size = 3, max.overlaps = Inf) +
  labs(title = "PCA CHECK: Combat-corrected, Aggregated Data",
       subtitle = "PCA of Gene Expression Data",
       x = "PC1 (Variance Explained)",
       y = "PC2 (Variance Explained)",
       color = "Condition",
       shape = "Cohort") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("RIF" = "blue", "Control" = "red")) +
  theme(legend.position = "top",
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5))

print(pca_plot)
```

DE analysis
```{r}
# Align final_dataframe columns with phenotype_data rows
filtered_data <- filtered_data[, match(rownames(filtered_pheno), colnames(filtered_data))]

# Check if there are any mismatches:
if(any(is.na(match(rownames(filtered_pheno), colnames(filtered_data))))) {
  stop("Some GSM accessions in phenotype_data do not match the column names in final_dataframe.")
}

# Convert the condition column to a factor (if not already)
filtered_pheno$title <- factor(filtered_pheno$title, levels = c("Control", "RIF"))

# Create a design matrix based on the condition (Control vs RIF)
design <- model.matrix(~0 + filtered_pheno$title)
colnames(design) <- levels(filtered_pheno$title)

fit <- lmFit(filtered_data, design)
contrast_matrix <- makeContrasts(RIFvsControl = RIF - Control, levels = design)
fit2 <- contrasts.fit(fit, contrast_matrix)
fit2 <- eBayes(fit2)

results <- topTable(fit2, coef = "RIFvsControl", number = Inf, adjust.method = "BH", sort.by = "P")
significant_genes <- results[results$P.Value < 0.05, ]

head(results)
```

  scale = "row",

  clustering_distance_rows = "euclidean",

Renaming and adjust age column (prep for covariate DE analysis)
```{r}
filtered_pheno <- filtered_pheno %>% rename(previous_transfers = characteristics_ch1.8)
filtered_pheno <- filtered_pheno %>% rename(age = characteristics_ch1.6)
filtered_pheno <- filtered_pheno %>% rename(embryotransfers = characteristics_ch1.9)

#adjust age column
filtered_pheno$age <- gsub("age:", "", filtered_pheno$age)
filtered_pheno$age <- trimws(filtered_pheno$age)
filtered_pheno$age <- as.numeric(filtered_pheno$age)

#define ageGroup column and classify each sample 
filtered_pheno$ageGroup <- cut(
  filtered_pheno$age,
  breaks = c(19, 24, 29, 35, 39),
  labels = c("20-24", "25-29", "30-35", "36-39"),
  right = TRUE
)
levels(filtered_pheno$ageGroup) <- make.names(levels(filtered_pheno$ageGroup))

# First, clear up N/A so all values are numeric (sub w/ 0) then remove the additional txt

filtered_pheno$embryotransfers[grepl("N/A", filtered_pheno$embryotransfers, ignore.case = TRUE)] <- NA
cleaned_values <- ifelse(is.na(filtered_pheno$embryotransfers), NA, as.numeric(gsub("[^0-9]", "", filtered_pheno$embryotransfers)))
filtered_pheno$embryotransfers <- cleaned_values

#Now, calculate the median of non-zero values and sub median for the 0s (originally the N/A)
median_value <- median(filtered_pheno$embryotransfers, na.rm = TRUE)
filtered_pheno$embryotransfers[is.na(filtered_pheno$embryotransfers)] <- median_value

```

****DE ANALYSIS LOOP WITH COVARIATES
```{r}
#Define your condition as a factor with the relevant baseline level
filtered_pheno$title <- factor(filtered_pheno$title, levels = c("Control", "RIF"))

#Identify columns that will be looped over
covariates <- c("biopsy_timing", "embryotransfers", "ageGroup")

#Prepare a list to store results from each model
results_list <- list()

#Loop over covariates
for (covar in covariates) {

  #Build a formula that includes 'title' (Control vs RIF) plus the covariate
  #'~0 + title + ...': will ensure separate columns for Control & RIF (rather than an intercept)
  design_formula <- as.formula(paste("~ 0 + title +", covar))

  design <- model.matrix(design_formula, data = filtered_pheno)
  # FYI: each time the loop runs for each covariate a new design matrix is generated so the final one within the environment will only list the last variable it dealt with 
  colnames(design)[1:2] <- c("Control", "RIF")

  fit <- limma::lmFit(filtered_data, design)
  contrast_matrix <- limma::makeContrasts(RIFvsControl = RIF - Control, levels = design)
  fit2 <- limma::contrasts.fit(fit, contrast_matrix)
  fit2 <- limma::eBayes(fit2)

  results_loop <- limma::topTable(fit2, coef = "RIFvsControl", number = Inf, 
                         adjust.method = "BH", sort.by = "P")
  results_list[[covar]] <- results_loop
}


#Loop to assess significant genes for each covariate
for (covar in covariates) {
  cat("\nTop genes significant in model with covariate:", covar, "\n")
  sig_genes <- results_list[[covar]][results_list[[covar]]$P.Value< 0.05, ]
  print(head(sig_genes))
}

```

PCA model for each covariate analysis
```{r}
# Loop over each covariate model
for (covar in covariates) {
  # 1.Get the DE results for the current covariate
  res <- results_list[[covar]]
  
  # 2.Filter for significant genes using cutoff
  sig <- res[res$P.Value < 0.05, ]
  
  # 3.Determining the set of genes to use for PCA
  #If 100 significant genes are available --> top 100 most variable among them
  if (nrow(sig) >= 100) {
    genes_sig <- rownames(sig)
    expr_sig <- filtered_data[genes_sig, , drop = FALSE]
    # Calculate variance for each gene across samples
    gene_vars <- apply(expr_sig, 1, var)
    # Order by variance (descending) and pick the top 100 genes
    top_genes <- names(sort(gene_vars, decreasing = TRUE))[1:100]
  } else {
    # If <100 significant genes --> use top 100 most variable genes overall (from whole dataset)
    gene_vars <- apply(filtered_data, 1, var)
    top_genes <- names(sort(gene_vars, decreasing = TRUE))[1:100]
  }
  
  # 4.Subset the expression data to these genes
  expr_subset <- filtered_data[top_genes, , drop = FALSE]
  
  # 5.Run PCA
  pca_res <- prcomp(t(expr_subset), scale. = TRUE)
  pca_plot <- autoplot(pca_res, data = filtered_pheno, colour = "title") +
    ggtitle(paste("PCA for covariate:", covar, "\n(top 100 genes subset)")) +
    theme_bw()
  print(pca_plot)
}

```





EXTRA:
BIOPSY TIMING CORRECTION
```{r}
# Isolate control samples from "cohort 2, batch 1"
control_samples_timing <- phenotype_data %>%
  filter(grepl("Control", title), grepl("batch: cohort 2, batch 1", batch)) %>%
  rownames()

# Prepare biopsy timing factor
phenotype_data$biopsy_timing <- factor(phenotype_data$biopsy_timing, levels = c(5, 6, 7, 8))
phenotype_data$biopsy_timing <- relevel(phenotype_data$biopsy_timing, ref = "7")  # LH+7 as reference

# Create design matrix for biopsy timing
design_timing <- model.matrix(~ biopsy_timing, data = phenotype_data[control_samples_timing, ])

# Fit linear model for biopsy timing effect
fit_timing <- lmFit(normalized_data$M[, control_samples_timing], design_timing)

# Correct ALL samples for biopsy timing
corrected_expr_timing <- normalized_data$M
for(i in seq_len(ncol(corrected_expr_timing))) {
  timing <- as.character(phenotype_data$biopsy_timing[i])
  if (timing != "7") {  # Only correct non-reference levels
    corrected_expr_timing[, i] <- corrected_expr_timing[, i] - 
      fit_timing$coefficients[, paste0("biopsy_timing", timing)]
  }
}

```
